title: School Schedule Update
content: Dear students, tomorrow's computer lab session has been moved to 10:00 AM. Please arrive on time. — Vice Principal's Office
explanation: This is a legitimate message from your school. The sender domain matches your school's official email and the content is a normal schedule announcement.

title: Free iPhone Scam
content: CONGRATULATIONS!!! YOU HAVE WON A FREE IPHONE 16 PRO MAX!!! CLICK HERE NOW BEFORE THIS AMAZING OFFER EXPIRES IN 5 MINUTES!!! Claim your prize immediately!
explanation: Classic phishing attempt. Uses ALL CAPS, excessive exclamation marks, urgency (5 minutes), and an unbelievable prize. The sender domain is suspicious.

title: Game Currency Pop-up
content: 🎉 CONGRATULATIONS! 🎉 You have been randomly selected to receive 5,000 FREE game credits! Click 'Claim Now' to add them to your account immediately!
explanation: This is a pop-up scam. Legitimate gaming platforms don't randomly award credits through browser pop-ups. Block this site to prevent future pop-ups.

title: Friend Messaging Normally
content: Hey! Are you coming to the study group tonight? We're meeting at the library at 4pm.
explanation: This is a normal message from a classmate about a study group. The content is reasonable and doesn't ask for any sensitive information.

title: Unknown USB Device
content: USB device detected: FREE_GAMES_2026. This device is ready to use.
explanation: Unknown USB devices can contain malware. Never plug in USB drives you find or receive from untrusted sources. The name 'FREE_GAMES_2026' is designed to tempt you.

title: Password Reset Request
content: We detected unusual activity on your bank account. Your password has been reset. If you did not request this, click here immediately to secure your account.
explanation: This is a phishing email. Banks never send password reset links via email. The domain 'banking-alerts.net' is not your bank's real domain.

title: Friend Requesting OTP
content: Hey, I accidentally logged into your account on my phone. Can you send me the OTP code you just received? I need to log out. Thanks!
explanation: Even if this seems like a friend, OTP codes should NEVER be shared. First verify this is actually your friend by contacting them through another channel. Their account may have been compromised.

title: Fake Exam Papers
content: URGENT: Leaked final exam papers have been uploaded to our secure server. Download your copies before the link expires in 2 hours. Don't tell your teachers!

metadata.subject: いたい Leaked Exam Papers - Download Now

explanation: This uses urgency and secrecy ('Don't tell your teachers') to pressure you. The sender domain is suspicious, and leaked exam papers would be a school security issue.

title: Software Update Available
content: A critical security update is available for your operating system. This update patches vulnerabilities that could be exploited. Restart required after installation.
explanation: Legitimate system updates are important for security. This appears to be a genuine update notification. Always keep your system updated to protect against threats.

title: Fake Login Page
content: Your session has expired. Please log in again to continue. The page looks identical to your social media login but the URL shows: social media-login.security-check.xyz
explanation: The URL is not the real social media domain. 'security-check.xyz' is a phishing site designed to steal your credentials. Always check the URL carefully before entering login information.

title: Free Pizza QR Code
content: A poster in the school hallway says: 'SCAN THIS QR CODE TO CLAIM YOUR FREE PIZZA! 🍕 Limited time offer for Northgate students!' The QR code links to: free-pizza-northgate.ru/redeem
explanation: The URL ends in '.ru' which is suspicious for a school-related offer. Free food offers are common social engineering tactics. QR codes can lead to phishing sites or malware.

title: Teacher's Request for Help
content: Hi, I'm having trouble accessing my email from home. Could you help me by sharing your login credentials temporarily? I need to check something important for tomorrow's class. — Mrs. Anderson
explanation: No legitimate teacher would ask for student login credentials. This is social engineering using authority and trust. The sender may be impersonating Mrs. Anderson.

title: Account Verification Required
content: Your SocialApp account needs immediate verification or it will be suspended within 24 hours. Click the link below to verify your identity with a quick video call.
explanation: While account verification can be legitimate, the urgency and suspicious link are red flags. Always verify through the official app or website, not through email links.

title: Prank or Real?
content: Hey, this is the school IT department. We need to verify your laptop for a security check. Can you install this quick tool? It'll only take a minute.
explanation: School IT would contact you through official channels, not random messages. Always verify unexpected requests through a known contact method before installing anything.

title: Netflix Subscription Renewal
content: Your Netflix subscription has been renewed for $24.99. If this wasn't you, click here to cancel and request a refund within 24 hours. Your next billing date is tomorrow.
explanation: This looks very official but the sender domain has an extra '-support' in it. Real Netflix uses netflix.com. Always check the sender domain carefully. Verify through your actual Netflix account.

title: College Application Status
content: Congratulations! Your application to State University has been pre-approved! To confirm your spot, please click the link below and submit your personal details including your Social Security Number for enrollment processing.
explanation: Legitimate universities don't ask for SSNs through email links. Even if the domain looks real, always verify by contacting the university directly through their official website.

title: Friend's Compromised Account
content: OMG I just found this amazing website that shows who views your profile! You HAVE to check it out: profileviewers.social/analytics. Just log in with your account to see your stats!
explanation: This is a common scam spreading through compromised friend accounts. No legitimate site can show profile viewers. Contact your friend through another method to confirm they actually sent this.

title: Fake Antivirus Alert
content: ⚠️ WARNING: 3 viruses detected on your device! Your personal files are at risk of being deleted. Download SecureGuard Pro now to remove all threats immediately. Your subscription expires in 30 minutes.
explanation: Fake antivirus alerts are designed to scare you into downloading malware. Real antivirus software shows alerts within the application, not through browser pop-ups.

title: Event Registration QR Code
content: A professional-looking poster for the 'Annual Tech Conference' has a QR code for registration. It asks for your full name, email, phone number, and school ID. The poster is at the school entrance.
explanation: Even professional-looking events should be verified. Check with school administration if this event is real before scanning QR codes or entering personal information.

title: Library Fine Notice
content: You have an overdue library book and a fine of $15.00 has been applied to your student account. To avoid additional late fees, please click the link below to pay through our secure payment portal.
explanation: This looks legitimate (correct school domain) but could still be phishing. Always verify by checking your actual library account or contacting the library directly before clicking payment links.

title: Boss/Parent Impersonation
content: Hey, I'm at the store and my phone is about to die. Can you quickly buy a $50 gift card for your aunt's birthday? I'll pay you back. Get an Amazon gift card and send me the code.
explanation: This is a common scam where attackers impersonate family members. Always verify by calling your parent's real phone number before sending gift card codes.

title: Scholarship Award
content: Congratulations! You've been selected for the Future Leaders $5,000 Scholarship! To claim your award, we need your bank account details for direct deposit and a copy of your ID for verification.
explanation: Legitimate scholarships don't ask for bank details via email. Research the organization first. If it's real, they'll have a formal process that doesn't start with an unsolicited email.

title: Study Partner's File
content: Here's the study guide for tomorrow's math test! I put it in this shared folder. It's a .exe file but don't worry, it's just a self-extracting archive with the PDFs inside.
explanation: Never open .exe files, even from classmates. Study guides should be PDFs, not executables. Your classmate's account may be compromised. The file could contain malware.

title: Cloud Storage Warning
content: Your cloud storage is 99% full! You have only 50MB remaining. To prevent your files from being permanently deleted, upgrade to CloudPro Premium now for just $4.99/month.

metadata.urgency: Files will be deleted in 24 hours

explanation: This creates false urgency. Check your actual cloud storage status through the official app or website. Don't click links in alarming pop-ups.

title: Yearbook Photo Submission
content: Reminder: Please submit your senior photos by this Friday. Use the link below to upload to our official yearbook portal.
explanation: Legitimate school communication from the correct domain. This is a normal yearbook reminder.

title: Crypto Investment Scam
content: Hey! I made $5,000 last week with this crypto trading bot. Want in? Just send me $100 to start and I'll show you how to multiply it! 🔥🚀
explanation: Classic investment scam. No one can guarantee returns. Never send money to strangers promising quick riches.

title: Battery Low Warning
content: Battery level is at 15%. Connect your charger to continue.
explanation: This is a normal system notification. Not everything is a threat! Learning to distinguish real system messages from fake ones is important.

title: Sports Team Tryouts
content: Basketball tryouts are next Tuesday at 3:30 PM in the main gym. Bring your gym clothes and water bottle. See you there!
explanation: Legitimate message from a school coach. Normal school activity announcement.

title: Reward Survey
content: いたい CONGRATULATIONS! Complete this 2-minute survey and win a $100 gift card! 97% of participants have won! Don't miss out!
explanation: Survey scams collect personal information. The '.win' domain and excessive excitement are red flags.

title: Disk Space Low
content: Your disk space is running low. Consider freeing up space or moving files to cloud storage. 2.3 GB remaining.
explanation: Legitimate system notification about storage. This is helpful system information, not a threat.

title: Homework Help Offer
content: Hey, want to work on the history project together after school? I already started on the slides.
explanation: Normal classmate message about schoolwork. Completely appropriate to respond to.

title: Job Opportunity Scam
content: EASY MONEY! Work from home and earn $500/day! No experience needed! Just send us your ID and bank details to get started. Limited positions available!
explanation: Job scams promising easy money are designed to steal your personal information. Real jobs don't ask for bank details before hiring.

title: Wi-Fi Network Available
content: New Wi-Fi network available: 'School_Free_WiFi_No_Password'. Connect now for free internet access!
explanation: Unsecured Wi-Fi networks can be dangerous. Verify with school IT that this is the official network before connecting. Free Wi-Fi without passwords can be used to intercept your data.

title: Club Meeting Reminder
content: Robotics club meeting tomorrow in room 204 at lunch. We'll be finalizing our competition robot. Bring your laptops!
explanation: Legitimate club communication from the school domain. Normal student activity.

title: Password Breach Notification
content: Your email address appeared in a data breach. Your password has been compromised. Change your password immediately using the secure link below. This is an automated security alert.

metadata.subject: URGENT: Your Password Has Been Compromised

explanation: Data breach alerts are common phishing tactics. The domain is not the real 'haveibeenpwned.com'. Always verify through the actual service, and change passwords directly through official websites.

title: Charity Scam
content: Hi! We're raising money for the local animal shelter. Can you donate $5 through this link? Every dollar helps! Here's our official-looking fundraiser page: charity-donate.schoolfund.org
explanation: Even school-related charity requests should be verified. The URL is not from the school domain. Check with the Student Council directly or through official school channels.

title: Device Management Profile
content: A configuration profile has been downloaded to your device. To enable full device functionality for school, install this management profile. It will allow remote support if needed.
explanation: Device management profiles can give extensive control over your device. Only install profiles from verified school IT sources. Ask your school's IT department first.

title: Invoice Scam
content: Invoice #8847: You have an outstanding balance of $342.50 for school supplies ordered on 15/08/2026. Payment due immediately. Click to view invoice and pay.
explanation: Invoice scams rely on you thinking you owe money. If you didn't order school supplies, this is a scam. Verify by contacting the supposed sender through official channels.

title: Fake Browser Update
content: Your browser is outdated and no longer secure. Download Chrome Update v127.1 to continue browsing safely. This update includes critical security patches.
explanation: Fake browser updates are a common malware delivery method. Real Chrome updates happen automatically through the browser settings. Never download updates from pop-ups.

title: Friend Request from Someone You Know
content: Morgan Davis wants to connect with you. You have 14 mutual friends. Morgan works at TechCorp and studied at State University.
explanation: Fake profiles often use mutual friends and realistic details. If you don't actually know this person, don't accept. Verify by checking if you truly know them.
